questions.stem: A nurse is preparing to administer digoxin 0.25 mg PO to an adult client diagnosed with heart failure. Which clinical assessment is a priority before administering this medication?

options.optionText: Measure the client's blood pressure in both arms
Auscultate the apical pulse rate for one full minute
Check the client's capillary blood glucose level
Check the client's most recent sodium laboratory value

questions.stem: A 68-year-old male with an established history of systolic heart failure is admitted to the telemetry unit with worsening dyspnea. Review the client's electronic health record exhibits (Nurses Notes, Vital Signs, and Diagnostic Labs). Based on these clinical cues, which action is the nurse's immediate priority?

options.optionText: Place client in high-Fowler's position and administer supplemental oxygen via nasal cannula
Administer 1,000 mL 0.9% Normal Saline IV bolus over 1 hour
Encourage oral fluid intake to treat elevated BUN
Schedule a routine echocardiogram for tomorrow morning

exhibits.title: Nursing Admission Assessment
exhibits.content: 10:00 - Client presented to ED in acute respiratory distress, stating 'I cannot catch my breath even when sleeping with 3 pillows.' Bilateral diffuse crackles heard in lower two-thirds of lung fields. +3 pitting bilateral lower extremity edema. Client appears anxious and diaphoretic.

exhibits.title: Vital Signs Flowsheet
exhibits.content:
BP: 168/96 mmHg
Heart Rate: 114 bpm (sinus tachycardia on telemetry)
Respiratory Rate: 28 breaths/min, labored
SpO2: 88% on ambient room air
Temperature: 37.1 C (98.8 F)

exhibits.title: STAT Laboratory Panel
exhibits.content:
BNP: 1,450 pg/mL (Normal < 100 pg/mL)
Sodium: 136 mEq/L
Potassium: 4.1 mEq/L
BUN: 28 mg/dL
Serum Creatinine: 1.4 mg/dL
Troponin I: < 0.01 ng/mL

questions.stem: A nurse on an inpatient surgical unit cares for a client on postoperative Day 2 following total knee arthroplasty who develops acute-onset chest pain and tachypnea. Which clinical findings support a hypothesis of Pulmonary Embolism (PE) rather than Atelectasis?

options.optionText: Sudden sharp pleuritic chest pain and unexplained tachycardia (HR 120)
Gradual low-grade temperature elevation (38.0 C) responsive to incentive spirometry
Diminished breath sounds at bilateral bases with dry nonproductive cough
Decreased urine output with clear bilateral lung sounds
